text: I think you should still benefit from energy hedging, as you discussed in the past, but how do you see the evolution of other costs, i.e., labor? [#406](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-406)
Since then, we have implemented a hedging policy for gas and electricity that protects us from market volatility. [#427](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-427)

Overall, this hedging strategy allowed us to stabilize a key component of our cost base and protect our margins in a very volatile energy environment. [#450](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-450)

Our hedging policy shielded us from energy costs, and the limited cost inflation we did see is being addressed through a dedicated cost-saving plan and targeted pricing actions. [#33](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-33)

Firstly, on the energy hedging policy that you've discussed, can I just check, generally speaking, across your markets, do you find that smaller independent peers are typically hedged also? [#601](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-601)

At that time, as energy prices were becoming extremely volatile, we decided to introduce a strict hedging policy for both gas and electricity in order to better protect the group from market fluctuations. [#436](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-436)

For the cost and -- in '25 in the guidance, so yes, we still have the benefit of our energy hedging policy, and we will save around EUR 30 million again in '25 in the total cost of energy. [#419](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-419)
The approach we follow is a layered hedging strategy. [#437](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-437)
And by the way, we need to keep in mind that the total energy costs represent 6% to 7% of the P&L -- of the top line in the P&L. [#614](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-614)

Overall, this layered strategy allows us to secure our energy costs several years ahead and smooth the impact of energy price fluctuation, which is particularly valuable in the current geopolitical environment. [#443](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-443)
The second question is about the saving on electricity and gas. [#581](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-581)

As shown on the slide, if we look at the situation as of year-end, energy volumes are almost fully hedged for N+1, around 2/3 hedged for N+2 and roughly 1/3 hedged for N+3. [#441](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-441)

So that's why we have decided to be more cautious and to, more or less, integrate in our balance of inflation, the positive evolution of the cost of energy [indiscernible]. [#494](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-494)

By the start of the delivery year, this means that energy purchases are close to fully hedged, which provides us with very strong visibility on our energy cost and significantly limits our exposure to short-term price volatility. [#442](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-442)
We are 93% hedged on gas and 94% on electricity for '26, 81% and 87% respectively for '27 and 61% and 53% for '28. [#76](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-76)

And for gas and electricity, we are also purchasing agreements in all countries so that we are able to hedge whenever we decided at group level. [#284](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003468571-284)

Energy, we are talking about deploying insulation systems, heat exchangers, also investments to try to stop using steam network and boilers to promote direct gas-heated equipment so that we save energy up to 30% to 40% doing so. [#319](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003468571-319)
As we discussed earlier, our gas and electricity needs are virtually fully hedged. [#458](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-458)
Let me briefly come back to the energy hedging strategy we implemented in 2022, shortly after the start of the war in Ukraine. [#435](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-435)
Can I just ask a quick follow-up on the energy cost? [#632](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-632)
First of all, on margin, could you quantify the amount of the cost savings you are mentioning? [#455](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003774119-455)
Do you have the 2025 energy cost, excluding vehicle fuel, to hand? [#635](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-635)
So basically financial savings and at the same time, CO2 savings. [#219](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003468571-219)

Energy hedging impacting more or less the regions, some one-off underlined [indiscernible] calendar effect in Southern Europe and lag to pass staff inflation in Latin America. [#142](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-142)

So for energy policy, hedging and so on, the situation on the market today, I would bet that majority of competitors have more or less followed that the way our strategy [ is public ]. [#608](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-608)
It was energy crisis, there was inflation. [#3141](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003468571-3141)
Turning to the next slide, you can see the concrete outcome of this hedging strategy. [#445](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-445)
I assume part of that is also getting that cost base inflation under control. [#334](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003512646-334)

So of course, we have the payback and it helps in EBITDA because when we invest in materials to make some savings in energy consumption, it can imply some CapEx, but some productivity gains also. [#464](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003394029-464)
